abstract:
We revisit Gagliardo–Uhlenbeck's expository paper on the family $\mathrm{KW}_	heta$ of Kapustin–Witten equations and make its $	heta$-dependence precise, with explicit constants. (A) For $	heta
otin rac{\pi}{2}\mathbb Z$, solutions of the two curvature equations (no moment map needed) satisfy the pointwise identity $|F_{\mathbb C}|^2d\mathrm{vol}=- rac{2}{\sin 2	heta}\,d\,\mathrm{tr}(\phi\wedge F_A- rac13\phi^3)$, whose primitive is global and gauge invariant; its boundary integral ($=\mathrm{Im}\,CS$) is invariant under complex gauge transformations. Hence solutions on compact manifolds with boundary are complex flat whenever $\iota^*\phi=0$, or $\iota^*(A+i\phi)$ is complex-gauge equivalent to a unitary connection. (B) If moreover $D_A^*\phi=0$, $\partial M$ is connected and $\pi_1(\partial M)	o\pi_1(M)$ is onto, then $\iota^*\phi=0$ forces $\phi\equiv0$ and $A$ flat, for every metric; instantons at $	heta\in rac{\pi}{2}\mathbb Z$ and abelian harmonic fields when $H^1(M,\partial M;\mathbb R)
e0$ show both hypotheses are needed. (C) With $m(	heta)=\max(	an	heta,\cot	heta)$: the sharp pointwise bound $|F_A-\phi\wedge\phi|\le\sqrt2\,m(	heta)|
abla_A\phi|$, and $\int_{B_1}|F_A|^2\le(1+4m^2)\int_{B_2}|\phi|^2$ with optimal constant at least $ rac{3}{16}m^2$. The printed constant $2(\cot2	heta+\csc2	heta)=2\cot	heta$ of their Cor. 4.7(b) fails for $	an^2	heta>\sqrt2$. (D) For $	heta\in(0, rac\pi2)$: $\int_{B_ho(x)}|F_A|^2\le256(1+4m^2)ho^2\int_{B_2}|\phi|^2$, so small balls fall below Uhlenbeck's curvature threshold with no smallness assumption on $\int|\phi|^2$; at $	heta=0, rac\pi2$ this fails (BPST). We also record the on-shell identity $ rac12\Delta|\phi|^2=|
abla_A\phi|^2+\mathrm{Ric}(\phi,\phi)+2|\phi\wedge\phi|^2$, fix orientation conventions for the Chern–Simons gradient flow, prove pointwise conservation of the moment map along it, and list respectful corrections (Cor. 3.3 needs "closed" and "complex flat"; Chern–Simons coefficients; Ricci signs). Novelty is modest: the results are elementary, and the known $	heta=\pi/4$ and closed-manifold cases are credited. verify.py runs 84 checks.

title: The $\theta$-family of Kapustin–Witten equations after Gagliardo–Uhlenbeck: a gauge-invariant local energy identity, a Dirichlet vanishing theorem, sharp $\theta$-constants, and some corrections
